response: {"text":"Earlier research comparing people who are deaf with those who hear has mostly focused on mental abilities, often concluding that deaf children score lower on average. Some investigations of physical skills gave mixed results, while other work suggested that both deaf and hard‑of‑hearing youngsters may show reduced initiative and signs of personality difficulties, such as higher anxiety, withdrawal, and submissiveness, with deaf boys displaying more emotional issues than their hearing peers. The present investigation aimed to contrast how deaf and hearing children living in residential care respond to a set of personality and interest questions. The sample included over one hundred deaf children from a dedicated school for the deaf and a similar number of hearing children from a residential school for dependent youths. Both groups were identified as having intellectual disabilities, allowing the study to control for intelligence and socioeconomic background."}
